158: A more transparent way to make sure that transactions are finalised at the
159: right time is to use `!with` `Connection.transaction()` to create a
160: transaction context. When the context is entered, a transaction is started;
161: when leaving the context the transaction is committed, or it is rolled back if
162: an exception is raised inside the block.

347: The `!status` property remains accessible after the transaction context has
348: exited, allowing you to check the final outcome of the transaction even after
349: the `!with` block has exited. This is particularly useful when you need to log
350: transaction outcomes or implement retry logic based on the transaction status.
